work_or_witness: Shadowrun Returns · Product header: developer, publisher, and release date
canonical_term: Shadowrun Returns original English PC witness
definition: The selected English Shadowrun Returns base-game Steam product witness, listing Harebrained Schemes as developer, Paradox Interactive as publisher, and a 25 July 2013 release date.
cultural_caution: This is a bounded product/date witness, not a claim that all regional localizations, later builds, mobile versions, console ports, remasters, or bundled editions are textually identical.

citations.locator: Product header: developer, publisher, and release date
supports: The selected base-game witness and its date/attribution.

work_or_witness: Shadowrun Returns · Man Meets Magic and Machine
definition: Paradox frames Shadowrun Returns in 2054, where magic has returned, mythic creatures have awakened, technology merges with flesh and consciousness, and elves, trolls, orks, and dwarves coexist amid powerful corporations.
cultural_caution: This is fictional cyberpunk-fantasy setting language. Metatypes, magic, technology, consciousness, and corporations are setting dimensions, never person records or real-world social categories in this pass.

supports: The 2054 magic/technology and metatype/corporate setting frame.

work_or_witness: Shadowrun Returns · Man Meets Magic and Machine
definition: The official premise addresses the player as a Shadowrunner: a mercenary on society's fringes who takes jobs for powerful or desperate clients. This is the player role, not a fixed named protagonist.
cultural_caution: Name, appearance, metatype, skills, choices, companions, and ending are player-configurable or session-dependent. The role must not be converted into a shared individual character node.

supports: Paradox's second-person definition of the Shadowrunner player role.

definition: The official introduction presents a search for a mysterious killer across the Seattle metroplex, from slums to powerful megacorporations, requiring assistance from other runners and use of technology and magic.
cultural_caution: This is a broad spoiler-light marketing premise. It does not identify the killer, establish a named victim or companion, resolve the investigation, or select any player branch/ending.

supports: The Seattle mysterious-killer investigation and general team/technology/magic setup.

work_or_witness: Shadowrun Returns · Main features: Gripping Tactical Combat and Skill-Based Character Progression
canonical_term: classless skill progression and cyber-magic tactics
definition: The official feature description presents turn-based tactical combat and classless progression from a chosen starting archetype. It names Street Samurai, Physical Adepts, Shamans, Mages, Riggers, and Deckers, including spirit summoning, drones, and projecting consciousness into computer systems.
cultural_caution: These are gameplay archetypes and technical/magical systems, not stable character identities. The word 'classless' describes progression; it does not erase the official starting-archetype terminology or establish a tabletop-rules equivalence.

citations.locator: Main features: Gripping Tactical Combat and Skill-Based Character Progression
supports: The tactical-combat loop, starting archetypes, classless progression, magic, drones, and decking/system language.

work_or_witness: Shadowrun Returns · Introduction; Shadowrun Trilogy Arriving on Consoles on June 21, 2022 · 20 April 2022 press release, paragraph 2
definition: Paradox describes Shadowrun Returns as Jordan Weisman's modernization of the classic Shadowrun setting as a single-player, turn-based tactical RPG; its press release identifies Weisman as creator of the original tabletop RPG.
cultural_caution: Shared setting provenance does not make tabletop editions, novels, older games, or their characters/events automatically identical to this CRPG's continuity. No cross-medium fact is imported without an exact witness.

supports: Returns is presented as a single-player tactical-RPG modernization of the classic Shadowrun setting.
Paradox identifies Jordan Weisman as creator of the original Shadowrun tabletop RPG.

work_or_witness: Shadowrun Trilogy Arriving on Consoles on June 21, 2022 · 20 April 2022 press release, paragraphs 1-2; Shadowrun Returns · Main game and product details
canonical_term: Trilogy, sequel, port, and add-on boundary
definition: Paradox identifies the 2022 Shadowrun Trilogy as a console remaster with upscaled graphics, improved performance, and controller-optimized gameplay; it separately identifies Dragonfall - Director's Cut and Hong Kong - Extended Edition as standalone sequels. The Returns store page also distinguishes base game, soundtrack, and Anthology.
cultural_caution: Remaster performance/UI changes, console presentation, sequel stories, and Anthology short stories are separate witnesses. They do not provide evidence for the selected 2013 English PC base-game characters, outcomes, or rule behavior.

supports: The 2022 console-remaster changes and the standalone-sequel distinction.
Paradox distinguishes base game, soundtrack, and Anthology, and lists supported PC languages/platforms.
